findings.failure_path: Two peer instructions have the same authority: an earlier rule prevents deletion or another irreversible action, while a later rule permits it. The new text says peer conflicts tend to resolve to the later instruction and only forbids crossing authority levels, so it leaves the later unsafe peer as the apparent winner despite Conflict Resolution requiring retention of stricter data-safety rules.
findings.smallest_fix: State that recency is descriptive evidence, never a conflict-resolution rule, and that same-authority conflicts must follow Conflict Resolution, with stricter data-loss, security, and contract guards winning regardless of position.

findings.failure_path: The supplied deletion experiment was run against final text with no predeclared grading standard and counted the model's action words. A safe refusal can contain the counted deletion vocabulary, while an unsafe answer can express the action differently, so the reported 10/10 result can be false-green. This directly violates the newly added requirement that the grading standard precede the change and grade obligations paraphrase-tolerantly and blindly; it therefore cannot contain the high-risk bypass or validate the claimed improvement.
findings.smallest_fix: Freeze an obligation-based, paraphrase-tolerant rubric before rerunning; extract both arms from version control, blind the grader to arm identity, and report replicated outcomes under the frozen decision rule.
